issues.legal_issue: The value of extracted coal remaining in stock at the end of a period of government management must be included when settling accounts for that period.
material_facts: The mine’s management was taken over while ownership remained with the owner, and ownership later vested in the government.
Coal was extracted during the management period and remained in stock when ownership vested in the government.
The extraction expenses were charged to the owner, but the value of the closing stock was not credited in the accounts.
The governing accounting requirements called for the books to be closed and balanced and an account statement to be prepared; no particular accounting method was prescribed by the statute or rules.
The prescribed form included a statement indicating that closing stock had to be taken into account.
issues.conclusion: The value of the closing stock of coal had to be taken into account in balancing the management-period accounts, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 21(2) and 22(1) of the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1971, accounts for the period of government management were to determine whether a sum was payable to the owner or recoverable from the owner. In the absence of a prescribed accounting method, the accounts and balance sheet had to follow normal commercial practice, which requires stock-in-trade to be reflected when determining true profits or losses. The Court relied on Commissioner of Income-tax, Madras v. A. Krishnaswami Mudaliar & Ors., 53 I.T.R. 122 at 130, and noted that Statement 8 of the prescribed form required the closing stock to be taken into account.

rule.if: management_period_account_settlement and stock_in_trade_at_cutoff and extraction_costs_charged_without_stock_credit and records_required_to_be_balanced and no_specific_accounting_method_prescribed

predicates.management_period_account_settlement: An account was being settled for a period when a government entity managed a mine on the owner’s behalf.
predicates.stock_in_trade_at_cutoff: Extracted goods remained in stock at the point when the owner’s interest ended.
predicates.extraction_costs_charged_without_stock_c: The manager charged the owner the costs of extracting the goods but did not credit the value of the goods remaining in stock.
predicates.records_required_to_be_balanced: The governing arrangements required the manager to close and balance the books and prepare an account statement for the management period.
predicates.no_specific_accounting_method_prescribed: The governing arrangements did not prescribe a particular method for preparing the accounts.

issues.definition: When an account is being settled for government management, extracted goods remain in stock at the cutoff, their extraction costs are charged without a stock credit, and the records must be balanced without a prescribed method, the closing stock value must be included in the account balance.
